name: AD Explorer Snapshot - Offline AD Enumeration & BloodHound
description: Sysinternals AD Explorer takes a point-in-time snapshot of the entire Active Directory database to a single file. The snapshot can be browsed offline (no further DC contact) and converted with ADExplorerSnapshot.py into BloodHound-ingestible JSON. A stealthy collection option: one legitimate-looking signed Sysinternals tool pulls everything, and all analysis happens offline.
notes:
=== TAKE A SNAPSHOT (GUI or CLI) ===
  # GUI: File > Create Snapshot, or CLI:
  ADExplorer.exe -snapshot "" C:\Windows\Temp\snapshot.dat /accepteula
  # Connect to a specific DC:
  ADExplorer.exe -snapshot "<dc_host>" snapshot.dat /accepteula

=== WHY IT IS STEALTHY ===
  # - Signed Microsoft Sysinternals binary (often allowlisted)
  # - One LDAP pull instead of SharpHound bursts
  # - All graph analysis happens OFFLINE from the .dat file

=== BROWSE OFFLINE ===
  # Reopen the .dat in AD Explorer with no DC connection to inspect objects/ACLs/attributes

=== CONVERT FOR BLOODHOUND ===
  pip install adexplorersnapshot
  ADExplorerSnapshot.py snapshot.dat -o bloodhound_out/
  # Produces users/groups/computers/etc JSON -> import into BloodHound
  # Objects-only (no ACL/edge processing) for huge DBs:
  ADExplorerSnapshot.py snapshot.dat -o out/ -m Objects

=== THEN ANALYZE ===
  # Import JSON into BloodHound CE, run PlumHound for reports

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  SharpHound / bloodhound-python   # direct collection (noisier)
  ldapsearch / ldeep               # targeted offline-able queries

recommended.note: SharpHound is the direct (noisier) collection alternative.
Import the converted snapshot into BloodHound.
Generate reports from the ingested graph.

defense.why_it_works: Any authenticated user can read most AD objects and attributes via LDAP. AD Explorer performs one broad, legitimate-looking LDAP read to a snapshot file; the heavy analysis then happens offline, out of reach of DC-side monitoring.
defense.prerequisites: Any domain user credentials; AD Explorer binary; network access to a DC.
defense.impact: Complete offline copy of the directory (users, groups, computers, ACLs, attributes) enabling full attack-path analysis without repeated DC queries.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1087.002/T1069.002] A single very large LDAP result set / full-subtree query from one host; AD Explorer process execution; 1644 (LDAP search) events showing a bulk directory read.
defense.artifacts: ADExplorer.exe on disk; a large .dat snapshot file; a single bulk LDAP query rather than SharpHound-style bursts.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=windows EventCode=4688 (NewProcessName="*ADExplorer*")
| table _time, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName has "ADExplorer" or ProcessCommandLine has "-snapshot"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
defense.prevention: Monitor for bulk/full-subtree LDAP queries (enable 1644 with thresholds); restrict who can read sensitive attributes; application allowlisting that flags Sysinternals misuse; reduce ACL attack surface so a full copy yields fewer paths.

detections.name: AD Explorer snapshot collection
detections.logic:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName has "ADExplorer" or ProcessCommandLine has "-snapshot"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
detections.false_positives: Legitimate AD administration/auditing with AD Explorer
detections.tuning: Correlate with a bulk LDAP read (1644) from the same host; alert on non-admin usage
